narrative: Your application was denied because the prediction estimated an 86% probability that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt. That does not mean failure is certain, but it means the assessment found a very high risk and used that as the basis for rejection. The strongest factor was your law school admissions test score of 24, far below the average of 37.18 among accepted students; this pushed the prediction most strongly toward failure. The second factor was your third-year class-rank decile of 3, compared with an accepted-student average near 5.79; this also pushed toward failure. The third factor was your undergraduate grade point average of 2.40, below the accepted average of 3.23, adding further weight toward failure. Your first-year decile, family-income bracket, and full-time status were not among the top drivers. The decision relied on these academic indicators, not on your gender or race. To move forward, ask admissions for feedback, invest in structured test preparation and retake the admissions test, strengthen your academic record with additional coursework if possible, and meet with an academic or bar-readiness advisor to build a concrete improvement plan before reapplying.
